## TL;DR

This turn addressed the latest review’s timing fallback finding. Board cards now pass the shared auto-repair hint the same state-time tooltip fallback used by other card statuses. When activity telemetry is missing or malformed, check-failure and merge-conflict retries still expose useful elapsed context. The new table-driven regression coverage passed, and the required scoped RepoOS check passed. The branch still needs a RepoOS-managed sync/review cycle: landability had reported conflicts and out-of-scope task bookkeeping changes, and the available sync command refused to run while this engineer turn was active.

## Work and rationale

The review pointed to a specific hole in the auto-repair path. `TaskCard.vue` already had a helper that prefers a valid `agentActivityAt` timestamp, falls back to `runningSince`, and then uses the task’s `updated_at` to build an “In this state” elapsed tooltip. The normal coding status used this helper, but `autoRepairHint` returned `retryHint` directly. That retry helper only produced a tooltip when an activity timestamp parsed successfully. As a result, both review-stage automatic repair cases could have a short status label without the useful timing popup whenever the activity fields were absent or invalid.

I extended the shared retry hint options with an optional `activityFallback`. `autoRepairHint` forwards it for each retry type, and `TaskCard.vue` supplies the existing activity/state-time helper. The fallback is used only when it can be produced and the real activity timestamp did not generate the active-time tooltip. This keeps valid telemetry preferred while making the missing-data case informative. The tests exercise both check-failure and merge-conflict retries through the common auto-repair API, so they protect the two review-stage call paths called out in the report.

I ran the required `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`. The first remote validation host hung and was removed by RepoOS; its retry on a second host completed successfully. The remote build and scoped test run passed. The local gate then passed staleness rebuild, formatting, lint, build, CSS/theme checks, rendered contrast, bare-require, task-asset, and UI smoke checks. The formatter was also run before that gate. The focused retry-hint test command passed all 13 tests, including the new table cases.

## Approaches tried

I first inspected the latest review report, branch status, relevant hint code, and `repoos landable 1058`. The report confirmed two outstanding work classes: the retry timing fallback, plus conflicts and unrelated task bookkeeping in the branch diff. I implemented the fallback by threading the existing card-level formatted fallback through the shared retry helper rather than duplicating timestamp formatting inside `retryHints.ts`. This avoids introducing a circular dependency because the card activity utility itself imports the retry formatter.

For landing scope, I attempted the supported `repoos sync 1058` command. RepoOS refused with “Task #1058 has an agent turn in progress.” I then attempted a manual Git merge only to establish whether the conflict could be resolved as directed, but the task-runner instructions prohibit manual staging and committing. I immediately aborted that merge. I did not finish an unsafe or partial merge. The previous dirty bookkeeping state was restored from the branch’s `main` ref for inspection, but that does not repair the ancestry conflict in the task’s existing commits.

## Challenges and blockers

The timing fix and checks are complete. The remaining blocker is repository coordination, not code: `repoos landable 1058` identified merge conflicts in the #1061 and #1070 task files and task-scope drift involving #1060, #1061, and #1070. RepoOS sync is currently refusing because this engineer turn is registered as active. The runner’s explicit rules also forbid using `git add`/`git commit` manually. Therefore I cannot safely produce the required synced branch in this turn. A RepoOS-managed sync after the active turn ends (or another authorized RepoOS workflow) is needed before a fresh review can pass. The reviewer also noted that an earlier Pipeline capture showed a paused row; the checked-in `board:pipeline` fixture explicitly clears the pause marker and marks its coding row running, but the capture should be regenerated from the final synced tree to provide fresh proof.

## Key learnings

When a shared status helper owns telemetry fallback behavior, derived retry statuses must use the same helper or explicitly accept its preformatted fallback. Tests should cover missing activity on every retry family that presents the derived status, not only healthy timestamps.

RepoOS landability catches more than source conflicts: unrelated task-file history can make a focused UI branch unmergeable or out of scope even when the current worktree is clean. The safe recovery path is RepoOS’s sync workflow, which preserves the required task-file rules and ownership of branch commits. If that workflow refuses during an active turn, the right result is to surface the blocker rather than stage a hand-built merge that the runner explicitly disallows.
